title: Status OK / Standby
fullDescription: A single flash on the diagnostic LED indicates the control board is powered and idle with no faults.
safetyWarning: Turn off power at the breaker before opening the unit. HVAC systems contain high-voltage components and refrigerant under pressure.

causes.cause: Component-level fault triggering 1 flash
Loose wiring or connector at terminal block
Control board failure requiring replacement
Sensor or thermistor out of calibration

symptoms: 1 flash displayed on diagnostic LED or controller
Unit will not start or shuts down quickly
Indoor or outdoor fan behavior abnormal
Reduced or no heating/cooling output

fixSteps.title: Power Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the breaker for 5 minutes, then restore power and observe whether the code returns.

fixSteps.title: Visual Inspection
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, open the service panel and inspect connectors, sensor leads, and contactors for damage or looseness.

fixSteps.title: Call Technician
fixSteps.instruction: If the fault persists after a reset and visual check, contact a licensed HVAC technician for component-level diagnosis.

repairTime: 30 minutes to 3 hours depending on root cause
whenToCallPro: Call a licensed HVAC technician if a power reset and basic inspection do not clear the fault, or any time refrigerant or sealed-system work is required.

faq.a: Only the power reset and visual checks are DIY-safe; component diagnosis or refrigerant work requires a licensed technician.
Typical service calls run $150-$500; sealed-system or compressor work can exceed $1,500.
If the unit is not heating or cooling at all, treat it as urgent. If it self-recovers, schedule service soon to prevent recurrence.
